audience: the parent who fills in every school, camp and sports form, with everyone's allergies, medications and insurance numbers kept only in their head
parents of more than one child, or of a child and an aging parent: the sandwich-generation caregiver juggling two stacks of papers
the parent standing at an intake desk trying to remember exactly when a symptom started
parents leaving kids with a sitter or grandparent who want one page that says what to avoid and who to call
people who already search for and save 'family medical binder', 'medication list printable', 'emergency contact sheet' and 'questions to ask your doctor' printables

visualWorld.setting: A warm home, not a clinic: the kitchen table, the fridge door, the bathroom medicine cabinet, the hall where the bag waits, and the moments that leave the house (an intake counter, a camp check-in table, the sitter at the door). Everything is paper a family keeps, drawn flat, on warm paper ground.

visualWorld.palette: The product's own rose on warm paper (definition.ts theme): accent #b23a5b, strong #86233f, soft #f9e3ea, wash #fdf1f4, ground #faf6f3, surface #fffdfb, ink #241a1b, borders #eaddd6 and #d5c3ba. People and tabs take PERSON_HUES (#b23a5b, #3f6fb5, #2f8a68, #b0791a, #7a55ad, #c25a2e) as quiet tints, a label for a person and never a health signal. One warm pop (butter or peach, via popFor) for magnets and sticky notes. Never clinical white-and-blue, never medical red, never a red cross.
visualWorld.mood: A kitchen-table record a parent keeps, calm and capable: the relief of having the answer in hand. Warm, tidy, slightly handmade; no alarm, no hospital, no glowing tech.

archetypes.name: Tabbed binder on the kitchen table
archetypes.clicks: The 'family medical binder' niche is built on binder sets with colour-coded dividers and sample pages (Kiddycharts, Sarah Titus dividers, Mom Colored Glasses' coordinating tabs per family member, Family Caregivers Online's 'sections using binder tabs'). A top-down binder with legible tab labels is the image the searcher already expects, so it reads as 'this is the thing I searched for' and gets saved as a reference.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-360: headline in the sans, 2-3 lines, left-aligned at x=64, ink on warm paper. 360-1220: kitchen-table ground with the open binder rotated -6 degrees, filling width 880, tabs running down its right edge (labels at 26-30px, readable on mobile); the open section's page shows 3-5 real labels. 1220-1330: one sub line. 1330-1500: product line (logo mark, name, price or 'free guide') aligned LEFT, nothing in the bottom-right 220x160 where Pinterest overlays icons.
archetypes.visual: Open tabbed binder, a pen and one small prop from the pin's topic (insurance card, stethoscope, pharmacy bag) on a wood/linen table.
archetypes.text: Headline; tab labels taken from real data (book section names in document.tsx, or RELATIONSHIP_LABEL, or the five printable names); 3-5 labels on the open page; optional sub from the pin description.
archetypes.bestFor: binder ideas, 'what goes in', care team / specialists, two-generation caregiver binder, '5 printables' lists

archetypes.name: The printed page, up close
archetypes.clicks: Printable sellers on Pinterest lead with styled mockups of the actual page (sample-page pins such as 'Free Printable Medical Binder and Worksheets Sample Pages'; mockup kits for clipboards and paper flat-lays exist precisely for this). Pinterest's own seller guidance says put the product front and centre. Seeing the real field labels lets the saver judge the sheet before clicking.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-300: headline. 300-1240: one US Letter page (or card) at 640x830 on a clipboard, tilted 3 degrees, centred-left, its block labels set large enough to read (24px min); a single highlighted element (a tick box, a footer note, a stopped line) gets a rose soft marker band and a thin leader line to a 1-line callout on the right margin. 1240-1330: sub. 1330-1500: product line, left.
archetypes.visual: A clipboard (or the intake counter, or a camp table) holding one of the product's five printed pages or a blank book page, with fill lines as grey strokes.
archetypes.text: Only the page's real block/field labels (generate*.tsx, document.tsx) plus one real line highlighted; headline; sub from the pin description.
archetypes.bestFor: shop pins about a specific printed page: Visit page, Intake summary, Forms sheet, Emergency card note, Symptom log, privacy footer

archetypes.name: On the fridge, in the wallet
archetypes.clicks: Emergency 'fridge sheet' pages are a staple of the niche (sold as their own page in emergency and caregiver packs) and the fridge is where the guide itself says the sheet lives. A recognisable home location tells the viewer where to use it, which is what makes an emergency printable feel worth saving.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Headline spans the top 0-320 across the full width over a soft wash band. The fridge door then occupies 320-1260 on the left (x 0-620), with the card/sheet held by a magnet at eye level (centre ~ y 640) at 420px wide; the right column (x 660-940) stacks the wallet with the card peeking out and the scissors on a dashed line, or 2-3 short 'where it lives' captions. 1260-1340 sub, 1340-1500 product line left.
archetypes.visual: Fridge door with a magnet holding the Emergency card or Caregiver sheet; a wallet or bag with a second copy; scissors on the dashed cut line.
archetypes.text: The card or sheet's real row labels (generateEmergencyCard.tsx, generateCaregiverSheet.tsx); optional captions from the emergency guide's 'Where the copies live'.
archetypes.bestFor: emergency card / emergency contact sheet, babysitter and grandparent sheet, 'keep it where you can find it'

archetypes.name: What to write, numbered
archetypes.clicks: Checklist and 'what to include' pins are the dominant guide format in this niche (question worksheets with numbered lines, binder 'what to include' posts, page-by-page inventories on bundle listings). A visible count promises a quick, complete answer and is saved as a reference to come back to. Pinterest and Tailwind both advise concise, legible type, so each line stays short.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-340: headline, large. 340-1260: 3 to 6 rows, each 150-180px tall: a number-badge (110px circle) at x=64, a 120px spot drawing beside it, and one line of real text (30-34px) wrapping to max two lines; rows separated by thin dashed rules. For 6+ items switch to a 2x3 grid of sticker tiles. 1260-1340 sub, 1340-1500 product line left.
archetypes.visual: Number badges with one small drawn object per row (bottle, ID card, calendar, phone, page), on warm paper with faint ruled-line texture.
archetypes.text: Items copied from the linked guide's ordered list or timeline (src/content/guides.ts), or the pin's own points; nothing paraphrased beyond cutting at a clause.
archetypes.bestFor: guide-linked pins titled 'What to write down', 'What to include', 'What to bring', checklists and timelines

archetypes.name: The medicine cabinet and the list
archetypes.clicks: Medication trackers and medication lists are among the most common pages in every medical/caregiver binder set found (Sarah Titus, Kiddycharts, caregiver packs on Etsy and Payhip). The open cabinet is the instantly recognisable home scene for 'what does everyone take', and setting the list beside the bottles shows the habit the guide teaches: check the list against the bottles.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-320: headline. 320-1240: open medicine cabinet centred, 760px wide: shelves with 5-7 blank-label pill bottles on the left, the swung-open mirror door on the right carrying the med-list-sheet taped inside (column heads readable at 24px); a checked-stamp overlaps the list's corner. 1240-1340 sub, 1340-1500 product line left.
archetypes.visual: Open cabinet, blank-label bottles, the medication list taped inside the door, a 'Stopped' fold or a 'Checked today' stamp.
archetypes.text: List column heads from document.tsx MedicalFactsPage; UI strings 'This list is right today', 'Stopped taking it', 'Checked today' from HealthPanel.tsx and medications.ts. No drug names, no doses.
archetypes.bestFor: medication list pins: what to write, last checked, stopped medications, 'bring the list'

archetypes.name: One record, many readers
archetypes.clicks: Bundle pins that fan out several pages and say what each is for sell the 'what's included' value at a glance (a pattern printable sellers recommend for multi-page sets). Pairing each page with its reader (sitter, camp, new doctor) is this product's real point of difference: different pages for different people.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-320: headline. 320-1180: 3 to 5 pages fanned in an arc from a single point near bottom-centre (each 300x390, rotated -18 to +18 degrees), each with its real title on its top bar; above each page a 90px reader prop (house-key = sitter, camp-backpack = school/camp, stethoscope = new doctor, fridge magnet = emergency card). 1180-1320: one short real caption under each reader or the sub. 1340-1500 product line left.
archetypes.visual: Fanned printed pages or person-cards, each with a small object standing for who receives it.
archetypes.text: Page titles from PrintablesModule.tsx docs; reader captions from the 'what to leave off' guide table; or relationship labels for person-cards.
archetypes.bestFor: what to leave off / privacy, five printables, sandwich-generation 'a card per person'

archetypes.name: From the drawer of printouts to one page
archetypes.clicks: Before/after is a proven Pinterest organisation format, and the listing's own problem is exactly that picture: 'a kitchen drawer of printouts and a portal you cannot open at 2am'. The messy top half is relatable; the tidy bottom half is the save. It also lets a shop pin show a REAL screenshot in context instead of a floating phone.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-280: headline. 280-760 'before' panel: printout-pile, sticky-notes, kitchen-drawer or two-stacks, slightly desaturated, on a darker warm band. A rose arrow or fold line at ~780. 800-1260 'after' panel: one clean letter-page, person-card, or phone-screen with a real screenshot, on bright paper. 1260-1340 sub, 1340-1500 product line left.
archetypes.visual: Messy paper (drawer, sticky notes, two stacks, bottles) above; one page or the real app screen below.
archetypes.text: Before side: wordless or real guide phrases (e.g. the questions guide's 'pile' notes). After side: real labels or real screenshot text.
archetypes.bestFor: 'typed once', 'bring the list, not your memory', camp/intake POV pins, caregiver two-stacks, shop pins with a real screen
